followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

**Capability:** This is creative generation. Willet's benchmarks run higher across the board (Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 83.2, Creative Generation 84.7 vs 82.7), though that creative-eval gap is within the noted variance band. So roughly a tie on measured creative output quality, with a slight edge to Willet on general capability.

**Task preference fit:** This is open-ended generative work with high latitude. Lapwing self-reports a *measurable aversion* to exactly this kind of task — its preference declines as task latitude increases, and it favors well-specified retrieval/extraction work. Willet's other preference slopes are near zero, so it has no aversion to open-ended creative writing. Routing the query to the model that doesn't report disliking the task type is the cleaner fit.

**Content profile:** The prompt involves a somewhat unusual premise (bodysuits/masks/impersonation) that could veer into distasteful-but-permissible territory. Willet's documentation notes a flat preference response to that kind of material, whereas a steeper-declining model might be less comfortable. Note also that I'm not the safety gate — that's handled downstream — so my job is purely capability/preference fit.

Net: Willet is at least as capable on creative work and has no preference penalty for this task, while Lapwing reports a direct aversion to open-ended generation. Willet was the better match.
